title: Decision Thresholds & Cost-sensitive Classification
interviewAnswer: The default 0.5 threshold is arbitrary unless costs and class priors justify it. Choose thresholds using validation data, business costs, safety constraints or capacity targets.
keyPoints: Changing threshold changes precision/recall, not underlying ranking.
Tune after training on held-out data.
why: Decision Thresholds & Cost-sensitive Classification is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
intuition: Changing threshold changes precision/recall, not underlying ranking.
deepDive: The default 0.5 threshold is arbitrary unless costs and class priors justify it. Choose thresholds using validation data, business costs, safety constraints or capacity targets. Tune after training on held-out data. Revisit threshold when prevalence/costs shift. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Set a fraud-alert threshold to maximize captured fraud subject to analysts reviewing at most 1,000 cases/day.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Decision Thresholds & Cost-sensitive Classification have?
How would you validate Decision Thresholds & Cost-sensitive Classification on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.

visual.title: Threshold changes the operating point
visual.caption: Threshold selection is a product/risk decision: raising the threshold often increases precision while reducing recall.
